question: Which award did Pakistani cricketer Sana Mir receive in June 2025?

options.text: Asia Woman Cricketer of the Year

solution:
The correct answer is __**ICC Hall of Fame**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The legendary Pakistani cricketer **Sana Mir** was inducted into the **ICC Hall of Fame** in **June 2025**, recognizing her immense contribution to the sport.
 
• She became one of the few women cricketers from **Pakistan** to receive this ultimate honor from the **International Cricket Council (ICC)**.
 
• **Sana Mir** served as the **captain** of the **Pakistan women's national cricket team** in both **One Day Internationals (ODIs)** and **T20Is**, leading the team with distinction for many years.
 
• In **October 2018**, she achieved the milestone of becoming the **No. 1 ODI bowler** in the **ICC Player Rankings**, which was a historic first for any woman cricketer from her country.
 
• The **ICC Hall of Fame** award is reserved for players who have demonstrated exceptional skills, character, and impact on the game over a long period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Career Profile and Background:**
 
 
• **Sana Mir** was born on **5 January 1986** in **Abbottabad**, **Pakistan**.
 
• She made her international debut in **2005** in an **ODI** against **Sri Lanka** in **Karachi**.
 
• Over her career, she played **120 ODIs** and **106 T20Is**, becoming a cornerstone of the national side.
 
 
 
• **Major Achievements and Statistics:**
 
 
• She was the first Pakistani woman to take **100 wickets** in **ODIs**, eventually finishing her career with **151 wickets** in the format.
 
• Under her **captaincy**, **Pakistan** won two **Gold Medals** at the **Asian Games** in **2010** (Guangzhou) and **2014** (Incheon).
 
• She is also known for her batting, scoring over **1,600 runs** in **ODIs** and nearly **800 runs** in **T20Is** as an all-rounder.
 
 
 
• **Post-Retirement and Influence:**
 
 
• She announced her **retirement** from international cricket in **April 2020** after a **15-year** long career.
 
• Following her playing days, she has remained active in the sport as a member of the **ICC Women’s Committee** and has gained popularity as a **cricket commentator** and analyst.
 
• In **2019**, she was awarded the **Asia Game Changer Award** by the **Asia Society** for her role in empowering women through sports.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Role of the ICC Hall of Fame:** The **ICC Hall of Fame** was launched in **2009** in association with the **Federation of International Cricketers' Associations (FICA)**. It celebrates the greatest icons of cricket history.
 
• **Linguistic and Cultural Impact:** **Sana Mir** is often credited with changing the perception of women's sports in **Pakistan**, encouraging a new generation of girls to take up cricket professionally.
 
• **Global Standing:** At the time of her **retirement**, she was among the top 10 most successful bowlers in **women's ODI history**.
